rv.q: It emerges as a touching reflection on the importance of friendship in the face of failure.
Pushin’ Thirty offers a fresh breath through a nostalgic heart of folk-styled music with an authentic tale which rejects melodrama for something easy to bite into.
Emma Rice’s steampunk reimagining of the Bluebeard story merges magic, song and wild glamour to create a glittering and enthralling cabaret of feminist resistance.
If it all ends up being rather inconsequential, it nevertheless has considerable charm.

cn.t: Critics praise this heartfelt two-hander for its evocative storytelling and deep affection for Dundee, with the play's songs and exploration of friendship and aging resonating warmly across reviews.
